[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

When a layer fans out into N sibling work items that share a once-per-container scaffold (an app shell, a cloud environment, a code component, a test harness), and that shared scaffold is not declared as an explicit prerequisite, every sibling appears independently dispatchable — so N builders (teams or isolated AI agents) each re-create, and collide on, the same foundation from a cold start.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Declare the shared scaffold as an explicit **foundation** that all siblings depend on (a T1 prerequisite), so the container is delivered as **foundation (1) → siblings (parallel) → tests**, never flat-N from a cold start. The foundation is declared in the logical architecture (before planning/export), emitted once (idempotent by its stable id), and reused as the prerequisite for every sibling.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Any container whose members share a once-per-container scaffold: a Presentation app (shell/providers/routing), a cloud environment (shared state/cluster), a code component (project skeleton), a test harness, or a cross-cutting foundation (AUTH/OBS).
- Especially when siblings are dispatched to **parallel/isolated agents** that cannot coordinate at runtime.
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Eliminates the cold-start collision (N agents scaffolding the same app).
- Makes the shared prerequisite an owned, gated work item instead of an implicit assumption.
- Produces a correct concurrency plan: the foundation is the critical-path predecessor; siblings then run truly in parallel.
page_texts.9:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Agentic and parallel delivery derive their value from concurrency. But concurrency is only safe when the shared prerequisites are explicit — otherwise the "parallel" work serializes badly (through merge conflicts and rework) or corrupts shared state.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Dependency graphs derived from behavioral/feature edges see feature-to-feature and data dependencies, but are **blind to the scaffold shared once per container**. That scaffold is not a feature and has no behavioral scenario, so it never becomes a node in the graph — and every sibling looks like it can start immediately.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Concretely: eight screen issues for one web app each carry only backend prerequisites (all satisfiable), so a planner reports all eight as concurrently dispatchable against an empty application. Eight agents each run `create-next-app`, install providers, wire routing, and set up the token pipeline — then collide on the same files. The same shape recurs for N microservices sharing a component skeleton, N infra concerns sharing a cloud environment, and N test suites sharing a harness.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- **Concurrency vs safety** — maximize parallel siblings, but not before the shared foundation exists.
- **Explicit vs inferred** — the foundation must be *declared*, not inferred from repo state at dispatch time (inference is non-deterministic and race-prone).
- **Idempotency** — re-running the pipeline must reuse the one foundation, not emit a second.
page_texts.14:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Treat the shared scaffold as a first-class **foundation** work item that every sibling in the container declares as a T1 (must-be-DONE-first) prerequisite. Declare it in the logical architecture; emit it once (keyed by a stable id); sequence the container as foundation → parallel siblings → tests.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
            WITHOUT the pattern                        WITH the pattern
   feature edges only (scaffold invisible)      explicit foundation dependency

   [screen A] [screen B] [screen C]  ...              ┌─────────────┐
       │          │          │                        │ FOUNDATION  │  (1, T1)
       ▼          ▼          ▼                         │  (app shell)│
   all "ready" — N agents each                        └──────┬──────┘
   re-scaffold the SAME app  ✗ collide          ┌───────────┼───────────┐
                                                 ▼           ▼           ▼
                                            [screen A]  [screen B]  [screen C]  (parallel)
                                                 └───────────┼───────────┘
                                                             ▼
                                                          [tests]
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation declaration | names the once-per-container scaffold in the logical architecture | logical architecture (precedes planning) |
| Foundation work item | builds the shared scaffold; emitted once (stable id) | the declaration |
| Sibling work items | each declares the foundation as a T1 prerequisite | the foundation |
| Sequencing gate | fails if a container has fan-out siblings but no declared foundation, or a sibling omits it | `/eap-sdd-health-check` (Phase 9/10) |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

At export, the planner reads the declared foundation and emits the T1 edge deterministically (it never infers a foundation from repo state). The foundation issue is emitted once — re-runs reuse it by stable id (idempotent). Siblings are dispatched only after the foundation is DONE; they then run in parallel; tests follow.
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

| Container | Foundation | Governing gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Presentation app | the app shell (framework scaffold, providers, routing/nav, token pipeline, BFF client) — the `kind: "foundation"` UI Contract | `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 9 |
| Code component | the project skeleton (`Foundation = Yes` in the component table) | Phase 10 Step 2 |
| Cloud environment | `IAC-FOUNDATION-<env>` (shared state/cluster) | Phase 10 Step 1 |
| Test harness | `TEST-HARNESS-<type>` (STD-APP-TEST-001) | Phase 10 Step 4 |
| Cross-cutting | `AUTH-FOUNDATION` / `OBS-FOUNDATION` | Phase 11 (seam cohesion) |
page_texts.20:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- A logical architecture that declares, per container, whether members share a scaffold.
- A planner/export step that reads declared foundations and emits T1 edges.
- Stable ids so a foundation is emitted once and reused.
page_texts.22:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#phase-1-declare]

#### Phase 1: Declare

1. For each container that fans out, identify the once-per-container scaffold.
2. Declare it as a foundation in the logical architecture (the appropriate marker per container type — see Variations).
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#phase-2-sequence-and-gate]

#### Phase 2: Sequence and gate

1. Emit the foundation as one work item (stable id); attach it as a T1 prerequisite to every sibling.
2. Dispatch siblings only after the foundation is DONE; run them in parallel; then tests.
3. On re-run, reuse the foundation by stable id (back-fill if adopting mid-flight).
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#example-ui-app-foundation-dependency-declared]

#### Example: UI app foundation dependency (declared)

```yaml
# Presentation app "dashboard": one foundation, screens depend on it
foundation:
  id: UIC-DSH-000        # reserve the -000 sequence so it sorts first
  kind: foundation
screens:
  - id: UIC-DSH-001
    dependsOn: [UIC-DSH-000]   # T1
  - id: UIC-DSH-002
    dependsOn: [UIC-DSH-000]   # T1
# planner emits: foundation (1) -> screens (parallel) -> tests
```
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Reserve a sortable id for the foundation (e.g. the `-000` sequence) so it orders first.
- Declare foundations in the logical architecture, never infer them from repo state at dispatch.
- Make the foundation idempotent by stable id so re-runs reuse it.
page_texts.27:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Implicit scaffold** — assuming the shared shell "will just be there"; it becomes N cold-start re-creations.
- **Inferred foundation** — detecting the scaffold from repo state at dispatch time (race-prone, non-deterministic).
- **Flat-N plan** — reporting all siblings as concurrently dispatchable against an empty container.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |

| Siblings missing the foundation prerequisite | 0 | Phase 9/10 |

page_texts.34:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** A dashboard app with eight screens dispatched to parallel agents.
**Implementation:** a `kind: "foundation"` UI Contract (`UIC-DSH-000`) declared the shell; every screen `dependsOn` it (T1).
**Outcome:** the foundation built once, then eight screens ran in parallel without re-scaffolding or colliding.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** Multiple infra concerns targeting one environment.
**Implementation:** `IAC-FOUNDATION-dev` declared once; each concern issue carried it as a T1 prerequisite.
**Outcome:** shared state/cluster created once; concerns applied against it without racing.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#scenario-1-mid-flight-adoption]

#### Scenario 1: Mid-flight adoption

A project already has some siblings built; on re-run the pattern back-fills the foundation declaration and attaches the T1 edge without re-emitting completed work (stable-id reuse).
page_texts.38:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#scenario-2-nested-foundations]

#### Scenario 2: Nested foundations

A UI app foundation itself depends on the AUTH foundation — foundations chain as ordinary T1 edges.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-008-foundation-before-fan-out-sequencing-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** When siblings share an undeclared once-per-container scaffold, N builders each re-create and collide on it from a cold start.

**Solution:** Declare the scaffold as an explicit foundation that every sibling depends on (T1); sequence foundation → parallel siblings → tests; emit the foundation once by stable id.

**When to Use:** Any container that fans out into siblings sharing a scaffold — UI app, cloud env, code component, test harness, AUTH/OBS.

**Key Benefits:**
- Eliminates cold-start collisions in parallel/agentic delivery
- Makes the shared prerequisite an owned, gated work item
- Yields a correct concurrency plan (foundation on the critical path, siblings truly parallel)

**Implementation Complexity:** Low

**Prerequisites:** Logical architecture that declares foundations; planner that emits T1 edges; stable ids for idempotent emission.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-GOV-004 (scaffold artifact), PTN-GOV-AI-001 (catalog), PTN-APP-API-040 (seam foundations).
